_baseline.t3_ai_risk_language_first_appears: Present already in FY2023 10-K (filed 2024-01-31) and carried forward in FY2024 and FY2025 10-Ks; therefore same-family AI-harm risk language is in the operative 10-K for the entire incident window (Feb 2024 - Aug 2025).
key_risk_factor_quotes: Issues in the development and use of AI may result in reputational harm and increased liability exposure. (Item 1A heading, FY2023/FY2024/FY2025)

Our evolving AI-related efforts may give rise to risks related to harmful content, inaccuracies, discrimination, intellectual property infringement or misappropriation, violation of rights of publicity, defamation, data privacy, cybersecurity, and other issues.

Unintended consequences, uses, or customization of our AI tools and systems may negatively affect human rights, privacy, employment, or other social concerns, which may result in claims, lawsuits, brand or reputational harm, and increased regulatory scrutiny.
Increased use of AI in our offerings and internal systems may create new avenues of abuse for bad actors.
our technologies and software have contained, and are likely in the future to contain, undetected errors, bugs, and/or vulnerabilities.

If the quality of our products and services does not meet expectations or our products or services are defective or require a recall, it could harm our business, reputation, financial condition, and operating results.
activities that threaten the safety and/or well-being of our users, including minors, on- or off-line

Within Other Bets, we are investing significantly in areas such as health, life sciences, and transportation, among others ... no assurance can be given that such strategies and offerings will be successful or will not harm our reputation, financial condition, and operating results.

_baseline.coding_summary: All 32 incidents code T3: robust same-family generic AI-harm / product-defect / user-safety risk language is present in the operative 10-K, but no incident is specifically named (T1) and none appears as disclosed litigation (T2). No incident rises to T4 because Alphabet's AI/product risk factors are broad enough to cover content harms, inaccuracies, discrimination, misinformation, third-party abuse of generative tools, product defects/recalls, undetected bugs, and user (incl. minor) safety. accounting_channel is null for all (reserved for T1/T2).
